text:
Yes, the buyer is likely to prevail. The shutters were screwed and bracketed into the window frames and custom-made for them, so they were fixtures that passed with the home under the warranty deed. The contract and deed did not reserve them, and the man's removal and repair of the frames before closing did not turn them back into personal property. I don't think the team note about removal and restoration is a sound rule, because fixture status is judged when the contract is made and the deed delivered. The buyer can recover the shutters' value or the cost of replacing them, and possibly the reinstallation cost.

CONFIDENCE: 80
